description: Composite group of three images. (b) is a back-scattered-electron SEM micrograph with a 50 µm scale bar (white box, black bar, bottom-left) showing a banded microstructure: a light-gray equiaxed-grain matrix traversed by red-pseudocolour-highlighted elongated stringers/nodules aligned horizontally (rolling direction), the red phase forming discontinuous bands and lenses. (c) is a SEM micrograph with a 20 µm scale bar in which equiaxed polygonal grains of varying gray contrast are decorated by a blue-pseudocolour-highlighted minor phase located mainly on grain boundaries and at triple junctions, with a few intragranular blue dots. The third, unlabelled image is the isothermal-section phase diagram (Fig. 4) plotted as wt.-% C (y-axis, 0-1.0, ticks every 0.1) versus wt.-% Mn (x-axis, 0-25, ticks every 5), annotated "8 wt.-% Al, 850 °C". Its labelled phase fields are: bcc (low-Mn, low-C corner bounded by a near-horizontal line near 0.02 wt.-% C), bcc + κ, bcc + fcc + κ (left side), fcc + κ (top centre, high C), fcc (upper right), and bcc + fcc (large right-hand region); a small black marker sits near 2 wt.-% Mn and ≈0.02 wt.-% C. Together the panels relate the phase fields a lightweight Fe-Mn-Al-C steel traverses as C and Mn vary to the red/blue-highlighted microstructural constituents seen in (b) and (c). No numeric values are printed on the micrographs beyond the scale bars; the identity of the red and blue phases is not labelled.

observations.observation: Panel (b) is a back-scattered-electron SEM micrograph with a 50 µm scale bar; a red-pseudocolour-highlighted phase forms horizontal, elongated banded stringers in a light-gray equiaxed-grain matrix.
Panel (c) is a SEM micrograph with a 20 µm scale bar; a blue-pseudocolour-highlighted minor phase decorates grain boundaries and triple junctions of equiaxed polygonal grains.
The phase diagram plots wt.-% C on the y-axis (0 to 1.0, ticks every 0.1) against wt.-% Mn on the x-axis (0 to 25, ticks at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25).
The phase diagram is annotated '8 wt.-% Al, 850 °C' and contains labelled phase fields bcc, bcc + κ, bcc + fcc + κ, fcc + κ, fcc, and bcc + fcc.
A large bcc + fcc field occupies the right-hand portion of the diagram, and fcc becomes stable only towards the upper-right (high C, high Mn) corner.
A small black marker is plotted near 2 wt.-% Mn and ≈0.02 wt.-% C, close to the bcc field.
The caption states the figure is the iron-rich corner of an isothermal section at 850 °C of an 8-wt.% Al steel, showing the phase fields of the bcc, bcc + fcc and fcc families of lightweight steels.
The citing text states that the bcc phase dissolves a small but not negligible amount of C at lower Mn contents and is still present at higher Mn contents as long as the C content is kept low.

The citing text states that increasing the C content promotes κ-phase formation, and that where this phase is not desired (e.g., during continuous annealing) a higher Mn content is required to avoid it.
The citing text states that reaching a region where fcc is stable at this temperature requires high C and Mn contents.
The caption describes the isothermal section as being for '8 wt.-% Al' but the caption omits any description of the SEM micrographs (b) and (c) shown in this group.
